names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 11 octombrie.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 11 Οκτωβρίου, «Αγίες Ζηναΐδα και Φιλονίλλα οι αδελφές», with the rank word left off.

The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2737, headed «Филонилла Тарсийская, целительница, мц.», with the rank word and the two epithets left off — of Tarsus, and «целительница», the healer.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 11. октобар ст. ст., „Св. муч. Зинаида и Филонида.“ — Св. is «saint» and not a rank and муч. is the martyr grade this corpus puts in `types`, so both come off and the bare personal name, the second of the heading’s two, is the whole of the form. **It is not the form any other book gives her** — a d where the Romanian’s «Filonila», the Greek’s «Φιλονίλλα» and the Russian’s «Филонилла» all have an l — and a copied script form goes in as the source prints it, untransliterated and unmended. `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM`.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 11 октября ст. ст. — «Мцц. Зинаиды и Филониллы (I).»
source.note: No rank is read onto her. Her line opens the day's second paragraph, which carries no icon; the day's two icons are both plain-service ones in the first paragraph, standing before the apostle Philip and before Theophanes of Nicaea.

attestations.note: Her index page is the one of the two that carries the healer's epithet outright, «Филонилла Тарсийская, целительница, мц.», and the life gives the art of medicine to both sisters, which is where the `physician` type comes from. The Russian also makes the two kinswomen of the apostle Paul, which neither of this folder's other sources said. The «(I)» is the first century and no year is printed, so no `dates` are proposed.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 11 octombrie — «Sfânta Muceniță Filonila»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 11ης Οκτωβρίου — «Αγίες Ζηναΐδα και Φιλονίλλα οι αδελφές»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 11 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same pair of sisters of Tarsus in Cilicia. The page argues against one piece of the tradition itself: some synaxaria say they were kinswomen of the Apostle Paul, but their names have nothing Hebrew about them and so, it says, that claim has no basis. It gives no year at all, so no `dates` object is proposed, and it adds the place of their death, a cave at Demetrias. It prints one apolytikion, which names them both and is taken here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 24.10.2026 (11. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Зинаида и Филонида.“

attestations.note: The day’s fifth entry, the second of its two names. The heading is quoted whole, with the closing full stop the Prologue itself prints, which is what BRIEF-SERBIAN section 4 asks for. It had to be measured off the raw cached page, because srbody.mjs and sr-cand.mjs both strip it from their printed output: every heading of this day ends ". " in the source. THE HEADING IS AN ENUMERATED COMPANY OF TWO, Зинаида and Филонида, so section 5 counts two names, two folders are owed a row and the corpus holds both. The quoted line is the one heading, whole, on both rows. The entry opens «Сестре рођене, родом од Тарса», own sisters of Tarsus, which is the kinship the two folders already relate each other on, and the city both display names carry. **THE KINSHIP WITH PAUL IS GIVEN AS A REPORT AND IS TREATED AS ONE.** «Називају их сродницима св. апостола Павла» — **they are called** kinswomen of the apostle Paul; the book does not assert it in its own voice. `paul-the-apostle` is already related on both folders, so nothing is added and nothing is claimed that the sentence does not claim. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND UNTOUCHABLE: both folders hold `dates: null` and **this entry gives no year, no reign and no emperor** — there is nothing here to infer from, and the appended paragraphs carry no four-digit year at all. With neither birth nor death on either folder, `date-audit`’s `stated` reads both lives’ prose. Measured after the write: unmoved. `types` UNTOUCHED at `martyr`, `physician` on both: муч. in the heading is the `martyr`, and «Знађаху лекарску вештину» corroborates the `physician`. **`virgin` is NOT added although the entry calls them девојке who renounced the world** — that is a word in a body and not a rank in a heading, which is the same refusal this range made for Eulampia on the Julian 10 October. No `office`, no `locations` — the cave the entry puts them in is «нека пештера», some cave, and no coordinate follows from that. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: **they were stoned, and by night.** «Но неки неверни нападну их ноћу и побију камењем» — some unbelievers attacked them in the night and killed them with stones. WHAT IS HERS: **the gift of wonderworking, and the entry gives its cause.** «Нарочито Филонида због великог поста удостоји се дара чудотворства» — Philonilla especially, for her great fasting, was counted worthy of the gift of wonderworking. **`wonderworker` IS NOT ADDED TO `types`**: it is a sentence in the body and not a rank in the heading, and the heading’s only rank word is муч. **THE FORM IS NOT THE ONE ANY OTHER BOOK GIVES HER, AND THAT IS NOT A CORRUPTION.** The heading prints «Филонида» where the Romanian stores «Filonila», the Greek «Φιλονίλλα» and the Russian «Филонилла» — a d where the others have an l, twice over. It is a copied script form and goes in as printed; `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for it and it folds to `филонида`, which is nothing else in the corpus. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S SECOND ENTRY IS REFUSED AND IT IS NOT A CLOSE CALL. «Спомен Седмог Васељенског Сабора.» — **a Council is not a folder**, and the entry is about the Council and not about a person: Nicaea in 787 under the empress Irene and her son Constantine and the patriarch Tarasius, 367 Fathers, the definition of the veneration of icons out of Scripture, the Fathers and attested wonders, and the ruling that relics of martyrs must be put into the antimension. It names the bishop Constantine of Cyprus, who told the Council the story of the shepherd of Constantia who struck the Mother of God’s icon with his iron staff, spoiled the right eye of the image, stumbled on leaving and put out his own right eye with the same staff. **None of those takes a row and none is in any prose of this day**: the Fathers of a Council are not a folder, an emperor in an entry is not a relation, and the subject of an anecdote told at a Council is further still from one. `tarasius-of-constantinople` has a folder and gets nothing from this day.

hymns.text: Τήν πολυθαύμαστον Ταρσόν τιμήσωμεν τήν ἐξανθήσασαν ἄνθη τά τίμια, τήν Ζηναΐδα τήν σοφήν καί Φιλονίλλαν. ἅμα δέ ἔχουσαι τῆς πίστεως τήν κρηπῖδα ἀσάλευτον, πᾶσαν τήν μυρίδα τῶν δαιμόνων κατήσχυναν. Διό καί σύν Ἀγγέλοις χορεύουσαι, ὑπέρ ἡμῶν ἀεί πρεσβεύουσιν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’ — the one hymn on the page of «Αγίες Ζηναΐδα και Φιλονίλλα οι αδελφές», and it names them both.

english.text: Let us honour much-wondered Tarsus, which brought to flower those precious blossoms, the wise Zenaida and Philonilla; for having together the foundation of the faith unshaken, they put to shame all the host of the demons. And so, dancing with the angels, they intercede for us always.
